calls.video_title: I Just Invested $20,000 into the Stock Market (Here is what I bought)
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 24 Nov). Bought Tuesday; layering into the iShares Semiconductor ETF instead of picking individual winners as the competitive landscape shifts. Top holdings fell hard in a month (Intel -40%, Micron -35%, Nvidia -31%, AMD -25%, Broadcom -10%). He has trimmed individual semiconductor exposure but is not bearish on the industry - advanced computing, memory, networking, custom AI chips and manufacturing equipment still offer enormous opportunity.
calls.base_case: Semiconductor earnings estimates hold while prices stay low, keeping valuations intriguing as he layers in.
calls.bull_case: The sector rebounds from the sell-off with memory, networking and custom silicon leading.
calls.bear_case: Earnings expectations fall significantly over the next few quarters, undermining the buy-the-dip case.

calls.thesis: First tracked. Semiconductor basket, down ~40% from its June peak; prefers SOXX over SMH for its AMD weighting (largest holding, then NVDA/MU/AVGO/INTC/TXN/ADI/QCOM/MRVL/NXP). AI demand unchanged while valuations reset.
calls.base_case: Base: diversified chip exposure instead of picking single winners.
calls.bull_case: Bull: AI/data-center/memory demand keeps growing; sector rebounds into 2027.
calls.bear_case: Bear: sector has lost hundreds of billions in market cap in weeks; uncertainty higher.
